## A World of States

- [Politics]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ domain of human behavior that concerns the use of power
- The [state]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ master political institution through which power is exercised

![Source: Wikimedia commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Flag_Map_of_The_World_%282026%29.png/1920px-Flag_Map_of_The_World_%282026%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

::: {.nonincremental}
- Today: $\approx$ 200 independent states in the world
- Virtually every human being is under state authority
:::

## Varieties of States

::::{.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

![Swiss federal palace in Bern](https://prod-aboutswch-hcms-sdweb.imgix.net/dam/en/sd-web/1JMHPoagqsPZ/politisches-system-uebersicht.jpg?auto=format&w=2048)

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

![Somali civil war (Source: Wikimedia commons)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Map_of_the_Somali_Civil_War.svg/960px-Map_of_the_Somali_Civil_War.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

:::

::::

- Some states provide public services, guarantee safety and protection (e.g., Switzerland)
- Others do not have full authority over thier territory (e.g., Somalia)
- Others have authority but exercise unchecked violence on their populations (e.g., European fascism, Rwanda 1994)

---

## Questions

- What is a state and what does it do? 
- Why do states exist and how did they evolve to the current configuration?
- Why these differences in states' governance and outcomes?

---


## Our plan for today

Two views of the state:

- The Social Contract View $\rightarrow$ external protection to permit social cooperation
    - Solve the problem of "horizontal" violence 
- The Predatory View $\rightarrow$ entrenches power of few over many
    - Create a problem of "vertical" violence
